scope: One real Lattice pure-inet result, produced by the 661499d2 release binary through `lattice pack lock` / `lattice pack run` with the pinned Noble worker, carrying a Mneme-computed `consumer_binding`, admitted and then refused by Mneme's `mneme_eval::inet::consumer` after each Mneme-owned binding is superseded separately.

mneme.published_commit_note: Mneme main after the run. Its crates/mneme-eval/src/inet/consumer tree hashes to the same tree_blake3 below with the same method, and its inet/mod.rs and crates/mneme-eval/Cargo.toml match the recorded build-input hashes, so the exercised consumer is the published one.

uncommitted_consumer.tree_blake3_method: BLAKE3 of the `b3sum` listing (`<blake3>  ./<path>` lines) of every file under the tree, paths sorted with LC_ALL=C; measured before the build and again after admission, unchanged

driver.description: Scratch crate outside both repositories depending on `crates/mneme-eval` by path; built with rustc 1.99.1 from Mneme's own dev shell (`nix develop git+file://…?rev=b9e5648…`) and Mneme's Cargo.lock (no version changes).
driver.workspace_setup: Workspace::create with a FixedClock; an entity and a source in project:cedar, a source in project:birch, a source in project:elm (4 records). Authorization: principal `e2e-agent` over {project:cedar, project:elm}.

executable.path_role: release `lattice` built from a clean 661499d2 checkout (its cargo dep-info names that checkout)

authoring.description: Documented library steps `lattice::inet::route::pack::author` and `lattice::inet::route::instance` called from a scratch crate depending on the same 661499d2 source by path (Cargo.lock copied from Lattice; differences are only removed dev/optional/workspace-member packages).

commands.result: workspace of 4 records; features x=3, y=2; wrote artifacts/score.ngraph, artifacts/score.vectors, arguments.json, binding-record.json

commands.command: lattice-author author RUN/pack $LATTICE_NOBLE_BIN && lattice-author instance RUN/pack RUN/artifacts RUN/instances.ncl

(same environment) lattice pack run --pack RUN/pack --confirm-trust-local --allow-license AGPL-3.0-or-later --allow-license LicenseRef-noble-lang-undeclared --lock RUN/pack.lock.json --instances RUN/instances.ncl --instance pure-inet-artifacts --method evaluate --arguments-json "$(cat RUN/arguments.json)" --confirm-read-only

commands.description: operation_data::Plane::open(store_path(data), data) + load_metadata + read_payload, as Lattice's own worker fixture reads published results; written create-only. Byte-identical to the stored payload file.

admission.method: Each scenario opens a fresh `cp -a` copy of the prepared workspace, so every binding is superseded separately; the binding record is reloaded from binding-record.json and the document is the exact retrieved bytes.

outcomes.note: integrity is decided before supersession, so a corrupted document is never reported as merely stale

observations: `lattice operation-data show <version>` on the same data directory exits 1 with `operation data store is not initialized`: the operation-data CLI opens its payload root at `<data_dir>/operation-data`, while `pack run` publishes under `<data_dir>/payloads` (src/operation_data/cli.rs:71 versus src/operation_pack/shell/execution.rs:121 at 661499d2). The document was therefore read through the library plane API, as Lattice's worker fixture does. This is a CLI retrieval gap, not a route or admission failure.
non_claims: One sequential local run of one computation with one attempt; no repetition, concurrency, multicore or device evaluation.
No live Mneme service, API session or product path: the check ran in a scratch driver over a scratch workspace; recall, ranking and memory operations still never call it.
Admission is point-in-time: each decision holds only for the state read at that call; a barrier landing after admission is caught by the next admission, not retroactively.
The Mneme consumer is uncommitted on top of b9e5648 and is identified only by the tree hash above.
Mneme does not check the producer's graph identity, counters or interaction count; the one-byte tamper is detected because the result disagrees with Mneme's oracle, not by a document hash.
Lattice's projection generation is not a Mneme binding; only snapshot, schema, authorization and erasure are covered.
No proof was replayed and no production deployment or default adoption is claimed.
